Tempo

TEM-poh (stress on TEM) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

the speed at which a piece of music is meant to be played

The dance instructor clapped her hands to set the tempo for the warm-up.

Worked Example

Halfway through the song, the drummer pushed the tempo, and the dancers scrambled to keep up.

Only the speed changed - the notes and the words stayed the same. That is the clue that tempo names how fast the music moves and nothing else about it.

How Tempo Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

pace

pace: the everyday word for how fast anything moves along; tempo belongs to music

speed

speed: how fast something goes

Antonyms

pause

pause: a moment when the sound or motion stops

silence

silence: no sound at all, and nothing to keep time to

How Strong Is It? — pace → tempo → beat

pace vs. tempo

pace vs. tempo: Pace is looser than tempo: pace describes the rough overall speed of any activity, while tempo names the set speed a whole piece of music is meant to follow.

beat vs. tempo

beat vs. tempo: The beat goes further than the tempo: the tempo sets how fast the music travels overall, while the beat marks every single pulse you could clap along the way.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — temp

root — temp: time

suffix — o

suffix — o: Italian noun ending

Put it together

Put it together: Tempo carries the old root temp-, meaning 'time,' with an Italian ending -o, because English borrowed it from Italian musicians: the tempo is the 'time' of a piece - how fast its moments go by.

Use the root in a new word: temporary

Use the root in a new word: temporary: The bridge repair is temporary, meant to hold only a short time until the new bridge is built.

Root Check

Word Choice

Tempo is at home in music: musicians set, hold, push, or drag the tempo. Writers sometimes borrow it for the speed of a game or a story, but for walking, working, or running, English usually reaches for pace instead - that is the giveaway between the two.
